main_text.p: רַחְצִי m. Lotio: Aff. סִיר רַחְצִי Olla lotionis mee, Psal.60. vers. 9.
רַחֲצָה f. Lavacrum, Ablutio: שֶׁעָלוּ מִן הָרַחְצָה Quæ ascenderunt de lavacro, Cantic.4.2.
רָחַץ Chald. Confisus est: Ithpeh. Præterit. הִתְרַחֲצוּ Confisi sunt, Dan.3. v.28. ה usurpatum ex Hebraismo, quod Danieli familiare.

רחק Procul, Longè, Longinquum esse, abesse, existere vel distare, Longè vel In longinquum abire, abscedere, recedere vel proficisci. Frequenter cum Præpositione מִן construitur. Præteritum. רָחַק מִשְׁפָּט מִפֶּנּוּ Procul recessit jus à nobis, Jesa.59. v.9. Infinit. בִּרְחֹק Quàm longè distat, Psalm.103.12. Futur. יִרְחַק מֵהֶם Procul erit ab eis, Proverb.22.5. Niph.Futur. יִרָּחֵק Procul amoveatur, Eccles.12.v.6. Vid. רחק. Pih. Præterit. וְלִבּוֹ רִחֵק Et cor suum procul amovet à me, Jesa.29.13. יְרַחֲקוּ אֶת־זְנוּתָם Longè amovebunt scortationem suam, Ezech.43.9. Hiph. אַחַי מֵעֲלֵי הִרְחִיק Fratres meos procul à me abegit, Job.19.13. Infin. הִרְחֵק מֵאֵד Procul abscedendo valdè, Josh.3.16. Fut. אַרְחִיק נֶדֶד Elongarem vagari, Psal.55.8. id est, Quàm longissimè evagarer & fugerem.

רָחוֹק m. Longinquus, Longinquum: Et adverbialiter, Longè, Procul: רָחוֹק יְהוָה מֵרְשָׁעִים Longinquus est Dominus ab improbis, Prov.15.29. Plur. רְחוֹקִים Longinqui, Jesa.33.13. Fœm. מֵאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה Ex terra longinqua, Deut.29.22. Plur. רְחוֹקֹת מִפְּךָ מֵאֵד Longinquis à te valdè, Deut.20.15. Chald. רְחִיקִין הֲווֹ מִן תַּפָּה Procul remoti estote inde, Esr.6.6.
רְחִיקִים m.p. Longinqui: רְחִיקֶיךָ Longinqui tui, vel, à te, Psalm.73.27.
מֶרְחָק masc. Longinquitas, Remotio: בֵּית דְּמֶרְחָק In

page.notes: Hebrew words are hard to read at this resolution; the vowel points and some consonants in the Hebrew forms (notably the headwords, the Chaldee forms and the Pih., Hiph. and Fut. forms) are uncertain and may differ from the printed text. The "9" after "vers." in the first entry is doubtful, it may be an "o" or a damaged figure. The Hebrew of the Chaldee form in the entry Procul remoti and the form after "In" in the last line are doubtful. The big initial is the Hebrew headword רחק, which is written as printed. The last entry is cut off at the foot; the word "domo" below it is the catchword.
